**Manual for app interface 0.2.0. Updated 27 November 2026.** This date describes the manual, not the latest scientific database update.

The Living SEB app helps you browse the curated literature and explore associations involving social, emotional and behavioral skills. The quantitative sections use the included correlation matrices; Review also includes papers retained only for the literature map. The app supports evidence mapping and exploratory synthesis. A dedicated meta-analysis may require additional searches, decisions about participant overlap and measurement, and a model tailored to the research question.

# Getting started

Use the navigation bar or the Home quick-start buttons. The three workflows are independent:

| Your goal | Section | First action |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Find and read an article | Review | Search or select filters, then select a row |
| Synthesize domain-outcome associations | Meta-analysis | Choose an outcome, then run the analysis |
| Specify a structural model | MetaSEM | Select variables, then click Get info |

The app loads the published GitHub `main` data when it starts. An app release and a data release can change separately. **About & Citation** shows the app version, the loaded article/matrix counts, retrieval time and analysis environment. Retrieval time is not the date of the latest scientific database change. Save the selected data and report to document your actual analysis.

## Articles, matrices and N

An article can contribute several correlation matrices. Some matrices share participants, and pair-specific sample sizes can vary. Counts of matrices are therefore not necessarily counts of independent samples. **Sum of reference Ns** adds the coded sample sizes for contributing matrices; it is not a count of unique people or an exact N for every correlation. Check the source notes before interpreting or reusing these values. The app does not deduplicate participants or replace missing correlations automatically.

# Meta-analysis

This section fits one multilevel random-effects model for each of the five BESSI domains against a single selected outcome.

## Select and estimate

1. Choose a **broad outcome grouping** and a **specific outcome** in the sidebar. You can restrict the data by age class and publication year.
2. In **Summary**, inspect coverage by skill and the **Included matrices** table. Counts and reference Ns are displayed as whole numbers. **Invalid values** counts observed correlations that cannot be analyzed because r is non-finite or outside -1 < r < 1, or the reference N is non-finite or at most 3. Ordinary missing correlations are not counted. The CSV download retains source values and gives the reason in `analysis_status`. DOI links in the source table open the corresponding publications.
3. Open **Meta results** and click **Run the meta-analysis**. A domain needs at least two usable matrices. A sparse or failed domain is reported separately, so other domains can still be estimated.
4. Read the main table: **r**, **95% CI (r)**, **p**, **Papers**, **Matrices (k)** and **Sum of reference Ns**. The summary plot shows the correlations and confidence intervals.
5. Expand **Model details** for **SE (z)**, **Tau-squared (z)**, **Q (df)** and model status. SE and heterogeneity variance are on the Fisher-z scale; they are not standard errors or variances on the displayed r scale.
6. Open **Forest plots** and choose a domain to inspect the contributing estimates, labeled by authors, year and matrix code. Values are labeled as r along a Fisher-z plotting axis.

Changing the selected outcome or filters makes the previous results unavailable. Run the analysis again before interpreting or exporting them. **Summary** downloads always refer to the current selection; an **HTML report** is enabled only for a successfully estimated, current analysis.

## Model

Correlations are transformed with `metafor::escalc(measure = "ZCOR")`. The model is:

```r
metafor::rma.mv(yi, V = vi,
  random = ~ 1 | paper_id / matrix_id,
  method = "REML", test = "t")
```

Estimates and confidence limits are back-transformed to r. SE and heterogeneity variances remain on the Fisher-z scale. The interface plots confidence intervals; it does not display prediction intervals. Reference Ns and documented sample overlaps require substantive review even when the model converges.

# MetaSEM

This section fits a **one-stage meta-analytic SEM** directly to the contributing study matrices and reference Ns. The optional pooled matrix is a separate exploratory calculation; it is not the input to the one-stage model.

## Select variables and inspect coverage

1. Select SEB domains/facets, personality traits and outcomes. Optional age and year filters apply to this section independently of Meta-analysis.
2. Click **Get info**. Inspect the number of articles and matrices, **Contributing matrices per correlation (k)**, **Sum of reference Ns per correlation**, and **Studies included**.
3. Expand **Selected variable codes and matrix checks** for the readable labels, codes and available-pair counts. Incomplete matrices retain their missing entries.

The app requires at least two contributing matrices overall and at least one reported correlation for every selected variable pair. Pairs with k = 0 prevent estimation. Warnings for fewer than three matrices per pair or a reference-N sum below 1000 are advisory, not automatic exclusions. These checks do not guarantee identification, adequate precision or a scientifically appropriate model.

## Optional pooled matrix

In **SEM matrix**, click **Get the meta-matrix** to run `metaSEM::tssem1()` with its existing defaults. Inspect the pooled correlations and plot, and download the plot as PNG if useful. This step is optional for one-stage estimation and for its report. Large selections can take substantially longer to fit.

## Write and fit a model

In the **metaSEM** tab, use the codes listed as comments at the top of the editor. Each line gives `code = readable label`. The list updates when the selection changes, preserving the model you have written below it. Lines starting with `#` are comments and do not enter the model.

For a small worked example, select **Self-management**, **BF Conscientiousness** and **Academic achievement**, click **Get info**, and replace the example model in the editor with:

```text
academicachievement ~ selfmanagement + conscientiousness
```

The editor supports regressions (`~`), variances/covariances (`~~`), factor loadings (`=~`) and parameter labels. A directed coefficient can be fixed explicitly, for example `academicachievement ~ 0.1*selfmanagement + conscientiousness`. Intercepts, explicit constraint expressions and defined parameters are not supported by this app editor; use R for specifications requiring them.

- **Automatic covariances:** the checkbox adds covariances among exogenous variables and among endogenous residuals. Exogenous observed variances default to 1 unless explicitly specified, independently of the checkbox. Inspect the effective syntax shown below the editor.
- **Measurement models:** switch automatic covariances off, specify the required covariances explicitly, and identify the factor scale appropriately. The [official lavaan syntax guide](https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/syntax1.html) explains the operators; the app implements the subset described above.
- **Fixed paths and variables without directed paths** are supported. Feedback loops are rejected because this correlation-model calculation requires an acyclic specification.

Click **Fit the specified SEM model**. The current one-stage settings are `RE.type = "Zero"`, `acov = "weighted"` and `intervals.type = "z"`: between-study heterogeneity is fixed at zero and intervals use Wald-z inference. This interface update does not change those settings.

## Read the results

- **Model fit** reports optimizer status and relevant warnings. A solution that fails the app's convergence/uncertainty checks does not enable the estimates or report.
- For a **saturated model (df = 0)**, global fit indices are not informative. Otherwise, the fit table shows chi-square, df, p, CFI, TLI, RMSEA and SRMR. Turning off automatic covariances does not by itself guarantee positive degrees of freedom or an identified model.
- **Model estimates** lists free parameters with estimate, 95% CI and p. Expand **Model details** for SE and z. Fixed coefficients remain visible in the syntax. Regression coefficients, factor loadings, covariances and variances are different quantities; they are not all Pearson correlations. No path-specific heterogeneity column is reported for this zero-heterogeneity model.
- **Residual variance / R2** is reported for endogenous variables where applicable. R2 is one minus residual variance divided by model-implied total variance. It is not reported when the outcome residual correlates with a predictor. Out-of-range values are retained and flagged, not forced to zero or one.

Changing variables or age/year filters requires **Get info** again and fresh estimation. Changing syntax or the automatic-covariance option invalidates the SEM results but does not invalidate a pooled matrix computed for the same data selection. These safeguards prevent reports from mixing an earlier fit with a new selection.

## Save the analysis

From **Summary**, download an **RDS list** or **ZIP of CSV files**. These preserve variable names, missing correlations, source information, reference Ns, pair coverage, current selection, model syntax and package versions. Each matrix CSV includes a variable-name column. The ZIP also includes the source table, coverage and completeness tables, and a text file with settings.

From **Report**, generate the HTML report after fitting a current, validated one-stage model. It includes selected data sources, coverage, effective syntax, diagnostics, estimates, technical details, R2 and references. The exploratory pooled matrix appears only if it was calculated successfully for the same selection. The report does not require pooling first. The data exports do not replace the fitted-model report or your scientific decisions.

# Literature review

Review covers all included articles, including review-only articles that contribute no active quantitative matrix.

1. Use **Search articles** to search codes, the **full author list**, titles, abstracts and readable coding labels, including fields hidden from the compact table. An author search finds contributions in any author position, even when the table shows only the abbreviated first-author citation.
2. Filter by **BROAD topics**, **Specific topics** or **Analyzed constructs**. Choosing a broad topic also offers a selector restricted to its specific topics. Topics describe the focus of an article; constructs describe what was analyzed, so a construct can be present without being a topic.
3. Expand **More filters** for sample context, SEB measurement, scientific contribution and study design. Multiple choices within a field match any selected value; different fields and the text search are combined. If no article matches, clear some filters or use **Clean selection** before trying a new search.
4. The compact **Included articles** table starts in article-code order and shows **Code**, abbreviated **Authors**, **Year** and **Title**. Click headings to sort, change the number of rows per page, and choose **Columns to show**. Code is always retained. Add the optional **Full authors** column when you need every contributor; it is hidden initially and is always included in text searches. Additional columns use horizontal scrolling instead of squeezing all columns into the available width. Rows scroll vertically inside a bounded table area (up to 45% of the window height); the column headings and horizontal scrollbar stay in place within that area. Short results shrink to their content.
5. **Click an article code** to open its DOI in a new browser tab. Underlined codes have a small external-link marker; articles without a valid DOI retain a plain code. **Click elsewhere in a row** to open the **article card** inside the app. It shows objectives, topics, analyzed constructs, instruments, abstract, DOI, data access and coding notes where available. Quantitative papers list their active matrix codes and reference Ns; review-only papers are clearly distinguished. After filters or displayed columns change, select a row again if necessary.
6. **Download the filtered data** exports every matching article and all coded fields, regardless of the visible columns or selected row. The UTF-8 CSV retains the underlying machine-readable codes. **Clean selection** clears search and filters.

Detailed filters search the available structured coding. The sidebar reports how many articles have detailed coding; missing coding should not be interpreted as evidence that an article did not analyze a construct.

# Resources, citation and reproducibility

**Resources** links to this manual in HTML/PDF, the two simple R tutorials, codebooks and data, the living results, preregistration and project site. Local checkouts open the newly rendered manual; a standalone deployed app links to the published manual on GitHub Pages.

**About & Citation** provides the project citation and a downloadable BibTeX entry. This entry cites the project, not a particular filtered analysis or data snapshot. Analysis reports include references for all contributing articles, using DOI/title matches and full coded bibliographic metadata for articles absent from the historical bibliography. If required reference metadata are missing, export stops and identifies the article instead of silently omitting it. A separate filtered-study BibTeX download is not provided.

For reproducibility, save the data export and HTML report, record your app version and filters, and document decisions about overlap and measurement. MetaSEM reports and data exports include metaSEM, lavaan and OpenMx versions. The revised app requires **metaSEM >= 2.0** and **lavaan >= 0.7-3**; restart R after updating packages. Local setup instructions are in the repository's [INSTALLATION.md](https://github.com/feracotommaso/living_SEB_review/blob/main/INSTALLATION.md).

## Common questions

**Why are there no matches?** Search text and filters are combined. Clear the selection, check whether detailed coding is available, and try fewer restrictions.

**Why is a model or report unavailable after an edit?** Re-run the relevant step for the current selection. MetaSEM variable/filter edits require Get info, then estimation; syntax edits require a new SEM fit.

**Why does a selected article have no matrix?** Some papers are included only in the review, or their matrix was superseded/excluded from the active quantitative data. Check the article card and coding notes.

**Why is an N different across sections or skills?** Different matrices can contribute to different variable pairs. N is the sum of coded reference Ns, with possible participant overlap and pair-specific missingness.

**Why does a large model take time or fail?** Coverage, identification, precision and convergence are distinct issues. Start with a smaller scientifically justified model, inspect diagnostics and save the data if you need a tailored local analysis. The app does not repair matrices or change the model automatically.
